method: Inspection of the existing PNG plus source at the pinned commit. No new browser, scene build, runtime object inspection, raycast attribution or source edit.

findings.observed: A tall faceted translucent white cone occupies the left-center foreground. Its hard silhouette competes with terrain and nearby combat space.

likelySource.confidence: high static compatibility; no runtime mesh identity captured
likelySource.reason: Mission startup calls spawnSteamVents(5) without a biome/profile check. It creates an open 12-sided ConeGeometry radius1.6, height8.5 with a white DoubleSide transparent MeshBasicMaterial. Its eruption reaches opacity0.75, matching the visible upright translucent cone and nearby metal/yellow grate. Locations and cycle times use Math.random, so the exact vent and phase cannot be recovered from this PNG alone.

references.scope: Vent placement, collar, grate and cone geometry

findings.alternativeAssessment: ReferenceEnvironmentMechanisms.buildSteamConduits also contains a white cone, but its conduit is wall-mounted, initially hidden, and the Val Verde profile does not select that builder. That alternative is weaker for this capture; it is not ruled out by a live object trace.
findings.followup: Capture vent mesh UUID/name, camera projection, opacity and cycle state in a future frozen browser run; compare eruption off/on from the same camera. Replace the faceted volume with a bounded soft plume or depth-faded material, retain a clear damaging-volume cue, and review which mission profiles authorize these original geothermal hazards.

findings.observed: Large opaque beige chevrons appear above or across insertion foreground rather than reading as subtle ground inlays; another chevron appears near the pod roof silhouette.

likelySource.confidence: high shape/material match with a concrete static elevation counterexample; no per-pixel runtime attribution
likelySource.reason: The wayfinding material is beige 0xc2b79d and its two quads form the same V silhouette. Quad corners call getElevationAt without a current layer. The legacy canopy rectangles return6.8 over a broad central region. Thus an insertion marking can be wholly elevated despite the existing guard rejecting height differences greater than0.65 inside a quad.

staticCounterexample.guardExplanation: All corners can receive the same legacy6.8 height, so maxHeight-minus-minHeight is0 and the quad is retained. This is a static call-chain analysis, not an executed scene measurement.

references.scope: Per-corner elevation and current inter-layer guard
Walk elevation delegates to registered surfaces and inherited elevation
Fallback to legacy height when no registered surface owns the point

findings.followup: In a separate patch, bind each marking to its intended route layer and actual supporting mesh/triangle rather than the unqualified legacy highest elevation. Cover a flat ground marking inside the canopy AABB and actual ramp/deck markings with CPU checks, then inspect the same insertion camera and both floor levels. Preserve the existing no-cross-layer guard and collision contracts.

findings.observed: Long brown overhead beams cross the camera framing, while a dark flat roof/platform and thin posts occupy a substantial lower foreground area. The cloaked player remains present, but the image does not establish clear views of nearby threats across all camera positions.

likelySource.confidence: high compatibility for the long beam family; medium for the foreground roof/platform
likelySource.owner: Val Verde canopy-bough set and communications/watchtower props
likelySource.reason: The canopy builder creates four brown BoxGeometry(2,.25,41) beams atY6.8, forming a large diamond around insertion. The same profile adds the communications shack roof at[2,2.6,10] with5-by5 dimensions and the watchtower platform near[8,5.5,6], matching candidate foreground solid silhouettes. Exact ownership of each visible pixel cannot be resolved from the PNG.

references.scope: Four canopy beams and their dimensions/poses
Physical boom collision deliberately hides no meshes
Grounded physical-contact filtering excludes many overhead visual surfaces
Third-person camera target and final physical boom resolution

findings.followup: Capture the actual occluder mesh names, geometry instance IDs and camera-to-player/primary-threat segments. Evaluate camera framing or a bounded occluder fade/cutaway for these specific large overhead pieces, while retaining physical surfaces, supports, impact collision and cooperative visibility. Validate walking below/on the canopy and the insertion exit before choosing a solution.

recommendation.releaseInterpretation: The existing UI report passed its stated control/state checks. This separate visual review keeps graphic/readability work open and does not convert those checks into a visual-fidelity certificate. No runtime fix is requested inside the frozen milestone.

limits: Only one already captured frame was visually inspected.
No mesh UUID, camera pose or weather random state was recorded for this image.
Static source attribution is probable, not a live-render identity proof.
The canopy height counterexample follows the source call chain; it does not claim all beige surfaces have been individually attributed.
No additional Chrome, build, gameplay test, source mutation, GPU measurement or external search was performed.
